content.contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with prior ICH, ischaemic stroke within 30 days, fibrinolysis, or platelet count <100 000/mm^3.

anticoagulant_drugs.UFH: Initial treatment: i.v. bolus 70–100 U/kg followed by i.v. infusion titrated to achieve an aPTT of 60–80 s. During PCI: 70–100 U/kg i.v. bolus or according to ACT if pre-treated with UFH.
anticoagulant_drugs.Enoxaparin: Initial treatment for ACS: 1 mg/kg b.i.d. subcutaneously for minimum 2 days and continued until clinical stabilization. If CrCl <30 mL/min reduce dosage to 1 mg/kg o.d. During PCI: if last dose <8 h before balloon inflation no additional dosing; if last s.c. administration >8 h before balloon inflation give i.v. bolus 0.3 mg/kg enoxaparin sodium.
anticoagulant_drugs.Bivalirudin: During PPCI: 0.75 mg/kg i.v. bolus followed by i.v. infusion of 1.75 mg/kg/h for 4 h after the procedure. If CrCl <30 mL/min reduce maintenance infusion to 1 mg/kg/h.
anticoagulant_drugs.Fondaparinux: Initial treatment: 2.5 mg/d subcutaneously. During PCI: a single bolus of UFH is recommended. Avoid if CrCl <20 mL/min.

antiplatelet_drugs.Aspirin: Loading dose (LD) 150–300 mg orally or 75–250 mg i.v. if oral ingestion not possible, followed by oral maintenance dose (MD) 75–100 mg o.d.; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients.
antiplatelet_drugs.Clopidogrel: LD 300–600 mg orally, followed by MD 75 mg o.d.; no specific dose adjustment in CKD patients. During fibrinolysis give an initial dose of 300 mg (75 mg for patients >75 years).

Associated Conditions: Platelet P2Y12 receptor (target of antiplatelet therapy)
Target for clopidogrel in acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and PCI
